text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- (Islamist-oriented) Movement of a Peaceful Society (MPS) says the party's support of the government's programme is conditional on some changes being brought to the agenda. MPS holds seven positions in the cabinet, including the industry ministry. Party deputies voiced opposition to some sections of the programme being debated in the National Assembly ahead of a vote of confidence.
- Sweeping changes are expected to shake up the financial and banking sector to help speed up reforms in the overall economy.
- Debates in the National Assembly on the government programme will be extended by a day after more deputies requested the right to speak.

- "Terrorists" shot at a van carrying nine passengers in Ain Defla province, southwest of Algiers, killing two and wounding the rest on Monday. A bomb exploded the same day on a railway in Blida region, south of Algiers, wounding three men carrying out maintenance work.
